I farm 10.1 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do this year is mostly based on what has worked on my land and what farmers around me are doing. For wheat, I will still sow in early October on the whole 10.1 mu after getting the field ready in the usual way. I do not want to cut fertilizer too much, because if wheat comes up weak in autumn or turns yellow at jointing, the yield loss is hard to recover. But fertilizer, seed, and pumping water all cost money, so I will not chase the highest input. I will use a common improved wheat seed that people around here trust, put part of the fertilizer as base, then topdress once when the crop is really taking off. I usually irrigate around sowing if soil moisture is short, then again at jointing and grain filling depending on rainfall and the well cost.

For maize, the turnaround after wheat harvest is tight, so I will not do heavy tillage. I will harvest wheat and plant maize right away in mid-June so I do not lose moisture or miss the season. I will use hybrid maize seed, because saved maize seed is not reliable. Maize on my land responds to nitrogen, so I will give a moderate amount, with most at planting and some later if the stand looks good. If summer rain is normal, I may only irrigate once or even skip one round, but if it turns dry at tasseling I will use the well because that stage matters too much for yield. Herbicide is worth it because family labor is limited and some people work off-farm, so I cannot depend only on hand weeding.
